newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL speeds cost-cutting to offset gas loss.
newsitem.headline: MOL speeds cost-cutting to offset gas loss.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt, which released its first-half consolidated results on Friday said speeding up rationalisation programmes already underway could partly offset negative influences on its full-year profit.

"(MOL) intends to partially offset expected negative tendencies with the acceleration of the organisation development and central cost-cutting programmes," the company said in a press release on Friday. @

MOL expects that the Hungarian government's decison last week to postpone energy price rises to January 1 from October 1, as well as higher than planned forint depreciation, to negatively influence 1996 results.
The delay in raising energy prices means that MOL's gas business will continue to make losses, a company official said earlier.
As 65 percent of the 6.9 billion cubic meters of natural gas came from imports, "domestic production could only partially compensate for such losses," MOL said. @
The average sales price of natural gas in the first half of 1996 was 11.1 forints per cubic meter, while average import price was 13.5 forints per cubic meter, the company said.

"MOL remains well positioned to maintain its dominant position in Hungary and expand abroad into new exploration activities and retail as well as wholesale petroleum markets within the region," Zoltan Mandoki, MOL's general director said in the press release. @

MOL's after-tax profit for the first half of 1996, according to Hungarian accounting rules, doubled to 6.5 billion forints from 3.23 billion forints in the same period of 1995, unconsolidated figures show.

IAS consolidated figures show a group after-tax profit of 10.07 billion forints for the first half of 1996, but this also includes a one-off cash payment of 3.84 billion forints from chemical company TVK.
Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt is widely expected to announce the second phase of MOL's privatisation this autumn. @
APV still has a 58.7 percent stake in MOL, with foreign investors having 30.2 percent, the rest being divided between employees, domestci investors, municipalities and the company itself.
"MOL remains firmly committed to the continuing privatisation of the company," Mandoki said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange MOL shares closed at 1,555 forints on Thursday.
